AbstractText.Label: Context
AbstractText.content: Obesity is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction in skeletal muscle. Increasing the plasma amino acid (AA) concentrations stimulates mitochondrial ATP production in lean individuals.

AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: To determine whether acute elevation in plasma AAs enhances muscle mitochondrial respiration and ATP production in subsarcolemmal (SS) and intermyofibrillar (IMF) mitochondria in obese adults.

AbstractText.Label: Design
AbstractText.content: Assessment of SS and IMF mitochondria function during saline (i.e., control) and AA infusions.

AbstractText.Label: Participants
AbstractText.content: Eligible participants were healthy lean (BMI, < 25 kg/m2; age, 37 ± 3 yrs; n = 10) and obese (BMI > 30 kg/m2; age 35 ± 3 yrs; n = 11) subjects.

AbstractText.Label: Intervention
AbstractText.content: Single trial of saline infusion followed by AA infusion. SS and IMF mitochondria were isolated from muscle biopsies collected at the end of the saline and AA infusions.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: AA infusion increased ADP-stimulated respiration and ATP production rates of SS mitochondria in the lean (P < 0.05), but not obese, subjects. Furthermore, AA infusion increased the uncoupled (i.e., non ADP-stimulated) respiration of SS mitochondria in the lean subjects only (P <0.05). AA infusion had no effect in any of these parameters on IMF mitochondria in either lean or obese subjects (P > 0.05).

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: Increasing plasma AA concentrations enhances the capacity for respiration and ATP production of muscle SS, but not IMF, mitochondria in lean individuals in parallel with increase in uncoupled respiration. However, neither of these parameters increases in muscle SS or IMF mitochondria in obese individuals.
